page.layout: One page of text, one column of verse, with a running head at the top centre and a page number at the top right. Below the text: a signature "A 2" at the right, then a woodcut fleuron (ornament, not transcribed). A closing word "LAMEN" sits at the lower left.

main_text.p: Iussos honores, & meritum decus, Ingrata ritus prætulit impios: Atque impotenti caca libidine, Sævisque lucri turpis amoribus Per omne præceps flagitium ruit.

Hac poena vindex, iraque Cœlitūm Veros timores mentibus afferat: Et contumacis damna superbiæ Horrenda monstrans, penitus opprimat Fastus feroces: inque animis nefas, Scelusq3 tandem mortiferum edomet. Vt dum renidet Lux Sapientiæ Cœlestis, & vox insonat auribus Diuina nostris: sedulus & doces Reposta culpis præmia noxiis: Et quanta celso laus manet æthere Iustum sequentes propositum greges, Terite pulsis criminibus procul Prompti sequamur perpetuum Ducem.

page.notes: Printed spelling kept as seen: "Hac", "caca", "Repofta" (long s rendered as s). "Scelusq3": the q carries a mark and a small 3, read as a -que abbreviation, doubtful. "Cœlitūm": the mark over the u is read as a macron. "LAMEN" at the lower left is faint and its first letter is partly lost in the scan edge, so the reading is doubtful. The fleuron below the signature is an ornament and is not transcribed. The verse lines are joined within each stanza paragraph as the layout rules require.
